articles.title: Ask HN: Social network with AI agents – why bad, why good?
articles.content:

That way, the agent can "process" far more information about people than the human, and help in building relations.Why it is a bad/good idea? Worth trying?

articles.title: Emu Concept – Make AI Follows Your Rules. (Feedback Wanted)
articles.content:
The idea is how can we make personal agent apps on the phone just listen to your rules... Like it's weird to have Muse, Grok Bot, Dots, Instinct not ask me about when I want them to work for me or align with my rules, values, and goals.If I give these agents access to tools/connectors/data they just "assume" what I want or what it should do rather than asking me? And even if I set these for a specific agent then what happens when a newer personal agent comes out? Do I have to reconfigure again my rules for each flavor of personal agents or harness?This is where our initial idea stems from and we need feedback:Emu is a self-learning on-device AI guardian that makes AI agents follow your rules. Also the video above kind of just highlights Emu's concept thought process.

articles.title: 索尼拒将《GT 赛车》上架 Steam：第三方开发者将《GT Sport》移植到 PC，支持 FSR 3.1 与着色器预编译
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，在索尼 SIE 宣布于 2028 年 1 月起取消新游戏的实体光盘后，近期有越来越多的开发者将 PlayStation 独占游戏以“数字游戏”的形式搬上 PC 平台。据 Wccftech 今日报道，虽然索尼至今未将《GT 赛车》系列移植到 PC 平台，但这一局面已被第三方开发者打破。名为“mlgprorektm8”的开发者在 GitHub 上发布了《GT 赛车 Sport》PC 移植版。这意味着，继《血源诅咒》和《战神 3 重制版》之后又一款 PlayStation 非官方移植游戏首次登陆 PC 平台。值得一提的是，该 PC 移植版不包含任何游戏资源，玩家需要自备正版游戏的 ISO 镜像文件才能运行。另外，该项目加入了 AMD FSR 3.1 帧生成技术，并针对着色器编译造成的卡顿进行了优化。该移植项目提供三种着色器编译模式，IT之家总结如下：第一种是“启动画面预编译”：游戏会在启动画面展示进度条，将此前在 PC 上使用过的所有着色器提前预编译。在这种模式下，首次启动时可能需要数分钟，后续启动仅需数秒。第二种是“新着色器编译时暂停”：当遇到从未使用过的着色器时，游戏会暂停运行（计时器同步暂停），并在左下角显示“正在编译新着色器”提示。第三种是“编译批处理”：在前一种模式开启的情况下，一次暂停可同时编译后续所需的着色器，提供短、中、长三档选项，分别对应最长 0.1 秒、0.3 秒和 1 秒的暂停时长（默认关闭）。该移植版还支持 AMD FSR 3.1 帧生成技术，但由于游戏本身不提供运动矢量数据，快速移动的边缘和界面元素不可避免会出现拖影问题。开发者 mlgprorektm8 表示，游戏在不同屏幕车辆数量下可维持 42 至 60 帧的运行表现，其测试平台包括英特尔 i7-13700KF 搭配 RTX 4070 Ti，以及 AMD 锐龙 5 9600X 搭配 RTX 3060。最新版本还引入了一系列性能改进，包括使用缓存内存处理栅栏写入、保存纹理查找结果以供复用，以及命令线程优先检查最近匹配的着色器配置，这些改动可将着色器搜索时间缩短约 30%。开发者目前正在开发多线程渲染器，以突破现有渲染器的性能限制。在官方层面，索尼对《GT 赛车》系列登陆 PC 的态度已趋于明确。索尼 2026 年 8 月发布的全新 PS5 广告重新启用了“Only on PS5”的宣传措辞，广告中展示了《漫威金刚狼》《沙罗周期》《GT 赛车 7》《战神：劳菲》《宇宙机器人》以及《羊蹄山之魂》等多款作品，其中《GT 赛车 7》此前从未推出 PC 版本。彭博社今年早些时候的报道指出，索尼正在收缩将未来推出 PC 游戏的计划，未来的大型单人游戏将重新定为 PS5 独占作品。PlayStation Studios CEO Hermen Hulst 曾在今年 5 月向员工表示，未来的单人游戏将继续保持主机独占。

Until next time!IT之家注意到，库克于 10 月 10 日开启中国之行，首站落地广东广州，现场观看使用苹果 iPhone 18 Pro 手机拍摄非遗咏春作品，记录传统文化。随后，他到访了北京、上海等城市，接受了商务部部长王文涛会见。此外，他还现身爱奇艺总部，由爱奇艺 CEO 龚宇亲自接待；到访清华大学，与腾讯董事会主席兼首席执行官马化腾、百度创始人李彦宏出现在央视《新闻联播》的镜头中；现身上海米哈游总部，由米哈游创始人、总裁刘伟（大伟哥）亲自接待。相关阅读：《库克卸任 CEO 后首次来华：首站落地广州，观看苹果 iPhone 18 Pro 手机拍摄的非遗咏春作品》《广东省省长孟凡利会见苹果执行董事长库克一行，库克称愿意进一步扩大在粤业务布局》《库克分享卸任苹果 CEO 后首次来华最新动态：与苏炳添喝早茶聊天、同 Xmind 思维导图开发者交流等》《苹果库克现身清华大学：参加经管学院顾问委员会年会，目前担任主席》《苹果库克现身爱奇艺总部，爱奇艺 CEO 龚宇亲自接待》《苹果库克、腾讯马化腾、百度李彦宏登上〈新闻联播〉，参加清华经管学院顾问委员会 2026 年会》《商务部部长王文涛会见美国苹果公司执行董事长蒂姆 · 库克，就人工智能发展等进行交流》《上海市委书记陈吉宁会见美国苹果公司执行董事长蒂姆 · 库克》《苹果库克时隔 3 年再次现身米哈游总部，与“大伟哥”见面》

articles.title: FADU 发布全球首款文件语义固态硬盘，支持加速器直接访问
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，韩国固态硬盘主控与方案企业 FADU 在 2026 OCP 全球峰会上发布了世界首款 FS-SSD（文件语义固态硬盘）。在传统的存储数据结构中，CPU 和操作系统负责文件搜索、权限管理、文件地址转换等任务，SSD 仅进行块操作，这意味着加速器若想访问存储文件需要通过 CPU 中介，带来了更高的延迟和 CPU 负载。FS-SSD 改变了这一情况：其内置文件处理固件，配套嵌入文件请求的 NVMe 命令，使得 SSD 能理解和管理文件，可直接同加速器通信，略过了 CPU、内存、软件层。FADU 计划将 FS-SSD 发展成为基于 DPU 的无主机存储服务器和可扩展文件存储解决方案。FADU 此次还展示了其 PCIe Gen6 SSD 主控 FC6161 "Sierra"。其性能达到上代产品的 2.5 倍；整盘顺序写入功耗＜28W，空载功耗＜5W；主控读取功耗＜6W、写入功耗＜7W。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，多年前曾有爆料称，育碧与腾讯旗下天美工作室群曾合作开发一款以中国古代为背景的《刺客信条》系列新作《刺客信条：命运》，但该项目目前已被取消。昨日，游戏媒体 MP1st 根据参与开发人员的作品集披露了早期玩法视频和截图，展示了潜行刺杀、信仰之跃，以及一款类似天机伞的旋转武器。这款作品原计划面向 PC 和主机平台，故事设定在公元前 206 年的秦朝。曝光素材大多来自 2025 年 2 月制作的原型，尚未达到完整游戏的开发阶段。曝光视频展示了一段任务流程：一名女性刺客需要进入一座遭历史人物项羽及其军队围困的宫殿，寻找一件神秘物品。片段还短暂展示了与项羽交战的首领战早期版本。这款游戏保留了《刺客信条》系列常见的潜行暗杀、跑酷和信仰之跃等玩法。其中一段画面展示了主角使用类似伞的旋转式武器。由于该项目当时仍处于原型阶段，游戏界面大多使用了占位素材，但我们仍可看到水墨风格的技能图标、生命值显示，以及带有阴阳图案的装饰条。其他动画则展示了一名男性角色通过跑酷动作接近并击倒敌人。MP1st 推测，游戏可能允许玩家选择角色性别，但目前没有官方信息证实这一点。值得一提的是，《刺客信条：命运》与另一款《刺客信条：侠隐》（Assassin's Creed Jade）是两个不同项目。育碧于 2022 年公布《刺客信条：侠隐》，该作同样是与腾讯旗下 Level Infinite 合作，同样以中国古代为背景，故事设定在公元前 215 年。育碧在 2026 年 3 月发布的系列动态中确认，《刺客信条：侠隐》仍在开发中，但尚未公布具体发售日期。据 MP1st 报道，天美工作室在 2025 年初进行组织架构调整，将工作室划分为四个团队负责不同项目。《刺客信条：命运》随即被取消。报道还提及天美曾开发的其他项目，包括代号 Athena、以希腊神话为背景的第三人称动作游戏，以及由《刺客信条：英灵殿》主导者负责的赛博朋克风格开放世界项目“ Invictus”，但后者随着天美蒙特利尔分部关闭而终止开发。

articles.title: 京东集团：坚决维护员工合法权益并向有关部门举报，坚决反对某些平台操纵舆论
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，“京东发言人”今晚发布声明，就近期一起员工被起诉事件表明立场。IT之家附原文如下：京东集团已关注到，近日我司员工在个人社交平台就大促节点在某竞对平台出现的异常舆论事件表达了相关看法，该竞对平台宣布对该员工提起多轮诉讼。京东集团坚决维护员工的合法权益，法务部将支持员工提起反诉，并向有关部门发起举报。在此，我们郑重声明：京东集团坚决保障消费者正当权益与知情权，坚决反对某些平台操纵舆论。相信事实与法律能够对此作出公正判断。京东集团2026 年 10 月 16 日结合此前报道，此次事件的核心人物是京东采销经理左琦。据观察者网 10 月 16 日报道，今年 618 大促前夕，左琦在朋友圈发布言论称，“不少商家和媒体都收到了某巨无霸流量平台公开指责京东的要求，只要这么干，就可以获得一次平台流量支持”，并配有一张带有今日头条链接的截图。相关内容随后被大量自媒体账号转发。抖音电商方面向时代财经确认，该案已由北京市海淀区人民法院以名誉权纠纷立案，并指出相关言论传播后，平台遭遇有组织的水军攻击，相关内容存在发布时间集中、文本同质化严重、IP 地址集中等特征。针对京东集团的声明，抖音电商于 10 月 16 日下午通过“抖音黑板报”账号发布情况说明。抖音方面表示，左琦被起诉后再次在朋友圈发布谣言，已对其最新谣言内容完成法律存证，并将依法追加起诉。抖音电商在说明中称，左琦所指文章系权威媒体基于“618”期间某商家与京东之间消费券争议的原创报道，多家媒体均有报道；所谓“没有评论”“被人为推上热榜”等说法不实，经核实该话题上榜时已有多家媒体参与讨论，置顶新闻下的实际评论数超过 100 条，相关新闻的打开率、互动量等指标均符合优质内容特点，属于自然上榜。左琦本人则在 10 月 16 日通过朋友圈回应。左琦称每逢 618、双十一等大促节点，商家和媒体便会收到针对京东的“爆料稿”，并质疑今日头条上阅读量仅约 1000、没有评论的稿件登上平台热榜，认为榜单存在人为干预。京东集团在今晚的声明中表示，将坚决维护员工的合法权益，法务部将支持员工提起反诉，并向有关部门发起举报。声明同时强调，京东集团坚决保障消费者正当权益与知情权，坚决反对某些平台操纵舆论，相信事实与法律能够对此作出公正判断。

articles.title: Linux 调频策略引发讨论：华为建议默认开启 CPU Boost，Arm 工程师提出异议
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，Phoronix 发现，华为工程师张鹏杰（Pengjie Zhang）昨日向 Linux 内核提交补丁，提议在支持相关功能的前提下默认启用 ACPI CPPC CPUFreq 驱动中的 CPU Boost 模式。为此，该补丁修改了 cppc_cpufreq.c 文件，新增了 20 行代码用于初始化 Boost 默认状态。ACPI CPPC（Collaborative Processor Performance Control，协作式处理器性能控制）是一套由 ACPI 定义的处理器性能控制机制，操作系统可通过它与平台固件交互，调节处理器性能。在当前通用 ACPI CPPC 驱动下，当处理器的最高性能等级（Highest Performance）高于标称性能等级（Nominal Performance）时，Boost 模式默认处于禁用状态，用户必须通过 sysfs 手动开启。Phoronix 指出，ACPI CPPC 驱动广泛用于 ARM64 Linux 服务器平台，而对于使用这些平台的用户而言更希望保持峰值性能。张鹏杰表示，只要有至少一个 CPU 支持 Boost，就应该自动为所有支持该功能的策略启用 Boost。不过，Arm 工程师、Linux 开发者 Christian Loehle 对此提出了不同看法。他认为，现代处理器的功耗和热设计约束太过于复杂，Boost 模式本身并不能保证处理器不会降频。我时常在想我们是否应该完全保留 Boost，如今芯片的功耗和散热边界已经足够复杂，以至于 Boost 的意义不大，它既不能保证不会降频，也不一定能获得请求的性能。他指出，懂行的用户可以自行通过 scaling_max_freq 单独设置性能上限，使其适应不同平台、工作负载和运行环境。Loehle 还提及，华为也曾引入过另一个相关 commit（54e74df5d76d），他对此的使用场景感到好奇，并认为在 Linux 上拥有一个标称性能不等于最高性能的平台目前只会带来更多麻烦。IT之家提醒：此次补丁针对的是通用 ACPI CPPC CPUFreq 驱动，并非面向所有 Linux 处理器平台统一开启 Boost。最终是否合并，仍取决于 Linux 内核维护者后续的讨论与审查。

articles.title: 2026 珠海航展门票 10 月 19 日 12 时开售：公众日 12 月 11 日起，个人票 600 元
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，今日，第十六届中国航展（2026 珠海航展）门票销售发布会在珠海举行，本届航展票务政策正式对外公布。门票将于 10 月 19 日中午 12 时启动售卖。本届航展全部门票实行实名制线上购票，一人一票、单次当日入场有效，由大麦 App 独家代理销售，现场不设售票窗口。观众可凭二代身份证、港澳居民来往内地通行证、台湾居民来往大陆通行证、外国护照等有效证件实名购票入场。IT之家注意到，本届航展采用分阶段错峰放票模式，自 10 月 19 日起设置 8 个售票日，每个售票日中午 12 时准时开票。今年航展打造珠海国际航展中心、莲洲无人装备展示区、高栏海上装备展示区“一展三区”全新格局，三大展区分时段开放，票价各有不同。珠海国际航展中心公众日时间为 12 月 11 日至 13 日。票种包含：个人票 600 元，优惠票 400 元；地面装备动态演示区套票（个人票 + 动态演示门票）1000 元，地面装备动态演示区优惠套票 800 元；太空中心专属套票 2499 元。莲洲无人装备展示区开放时间为 12 月 8 日至 10 日，单人门票售价 100 元，观众可提前探访前沿无人装备成果。高栏海上装备展示区开放时段为 12 月 7 日至 11 日，展区免费向公众开放，采取线上预约制，预约方式后续将由官方发布。第十六届中国航展（2026 珠海航展）将于 2026 年 12 月 7 日至 13 日在广东珠海举办。据介绍，本届航展不仅是一场世界级航空航天盛会，也是一场国际性航空航天及防务盛会，中国空军、海军多型新型装备将同台亮相，新质战斗力建设成果成体系呈现，充分展现人民军队开放自信、捍卫和平的良好形象。

articles.title: 微软秘密测试“Project Odeon”新应用，界面与 Win11 设置几乎一致
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，Windows Latest 今日报道称，微软正在测试一款代号为“Project Odeon”的应用。该应用通过微软商店分发，采用与 Windows 11 系统“设置”几乎相同的界面和图标。据 Windows Latest 实测，这款应用暂时不会取代“设置”，而是可以与其并行运行。微软尚未正式公布该项目，也没有确认是否计划面向公众发布。目前，Project Odeon 在微软商店中被标记为“Preview”（预览版），发布者为 Microsoft Corporation，版本号为 1.0.9.0。该应用要求 Windows 11 版本号为 26100 或更高的系统，并且在测试中需要启用开发模式才能安装。Windows Latest 在运行 Build 26340.9616 的 Hyper-V 虚拟机中进行了测试。结果显示，Project Odeon 能够读取电脑名称、网络状态和待安装的 Windows 更新等信息，但部分数据与系统原有的“设置”应用不一致。例如，在“关于”页面中，Project Odeon 显示存储容量为 125.9GB，而系统原有的“设置”显示容量为 381GB，其中已使用 68GB。另外，该应用还存在部分页面未完成、链接不可用等问题。这款应用还内置了隐藏的预览模式。通过启动参数 --preview 可进入包含虚拟账户、模拟硬件信息、示例设置和六张虚拟壁纸的测试环境。该模式下的一切都是假的，随意更改也不会影响 Windows 实际设置。其主页会显示一个名为“Microsoft Dev Box AMD 16vCPU/64GB/2048GB”的设备，名为“Enterprise-Preview-PC”；设备信息卡列出了一个 64 核 AMD EPYC 7763 处理器、64GB 内存和 build 26694.5000 的配置；而“关于”页面则切显示为一个“Preview 8-core” 处理器和 32GB 内存的配置。甚至连 Windows 信息部分也被标记为“预览设备”。从安装包文件来看，Project Odeon 还包含多个辅助程序，涉及账户管理、打印机设置、电脑重命名、时区调整、启动应用管理和卸载更新等功能。Windows Latest 据此推测，微软可能正在尝试将部分系统设置界面与底层操作拆分，使应用通过独立的辅助组件执行需要更高权限的任务。目前，微软尚未公布 Project Odeon 的正式用途、公开发布时间，也没有确认它会取代现有“设置”应用或加速控制面板退役。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，长鑫科技今日发布 2026 年前三季度（2026 年 1 月～2026 年 9 月）业绩预告报告：营业总收入：2650 亿元 ~2700 亿元，同比预增 725.96%~741.54%归母净利润：1310 亿元 ~1325 亿元，同比扭亏为盈 AI 解读本次业绩预告大幅超出市场预期，业绩实现爆发式增长。公司主营业务与财报亮点长鑫科技主要从事 DRAM 存储芯片的研发、生产和销售，是国内 DRAM 行业核心企业。本次 2026 年前三季度预计实现营业收入 2650 亿元至 2700 亿元，同比上年增加 2329.16 亿元至 2379.16 亿元；预计归属于上市公司股东的净利润 1310 亿元至 1325 亿元，同比上年增加 1362.8 亿元至 1377.8 亿元，去年同期归母净利润为净亏损 52.8 亿元。业绩增长核心原因2025 年下半年以来 AI 算力需求快速增长，全球 DRAM 行业景气度大幅提升，产品供不应求、价格大幅上涨；公司稳步推进产能建设、产品研发和工艺技术提升，单位晶圆产出和产能利用率持续提高，规模效应逐步显现；同时公司优化运营管理、拓展市场，深化产业链上下游协同，推动业务规模快速扩张，推动整体业绩显著提升。风险提示与说明本次业绩预告为财务部门初步测算结果，尚未经注册会计师审计，具体准确财务数据请以公司正式披露的 2026 年第三季度报告为准，投资者请注意投资风险。相关阅读： 《德明利 2026 年前三季度预计归母净利润 86.5~89.5 亿元，预计同比增长 32046.52%~33154.49%》《沐曦股份 2026 年三季度归母净利润 5.87 亿元 ~7.17 亿元，同比扭亏为盈》《海光信息 2026 年三季度归母净利润 27.1~29.8 亿元，预计同比增长 38.16%~51.93%》《中科曙光 2026 年三季度归母净利润 17.24 亿元，同比增长 78.48%》《江波龙 2026 年三季度归母净利润 140~149 亿元，预计同比增长 1864.55%~1990.84%》《长鑫科技 2026 年上半年归母净利润 776.05 亿元，同比扭亏为盈》风险提示：本文内容由 AI 自动分析生成，仅供参考，不代表IT之家观点。如有出入请以证监会指定上市公司信息披露平台为准。本文内容不构成投资建议，如有投资者据此操作，风险自担，IT之家对此不承担任何责任。

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20665v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can solve complex interactive tasks, yet reasoning and tool calls take time. In continuously changing environments, an otherwise correct action may arrive too late. We introduce RealtimeBench, with 180 tasks across six game types, to evaluate agents while games continue running during inference. Paired evaluations show that GPT-6.1-sol outperforms the faster Jev when games are paused, but falls behind when they keep running. The student acts without teacher calls during gameplay, and validation scores determine which updates are adopted. articles.content:

Abstract: Rapid advances in AI capabilities are causing benchmarks to saturate. Once several models approach perfect scores, a benchmark loses its power to differentiate between them, and with it its utility for informing AI safety cases and frontier policies. Yet benchmark items produce far more information than the scores we typically extract from them: a full transcript of how each model solved the task. We investigate whether these transcripts can be used to assess model capabilities even after benchmark scores have saturated. Abstract: Reward-guided discrete diffusion enables test-time alignment with downstream objectives, but applying Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) guidance at every denoising step is computationally expensive. Abstract: Agents pair reasoning models with harnesses that organize model calls, execute tools, load skill instructions, and retain history in memory. Abstract: Correctness feedback suppresses the very evidence that specification-completeness auditing is designed to uncover: programs that satisfy a written contract but violate intended behavior. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20679v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Representation-based safety defenses for vision-language models (VLMs) often learn to separate harmful from benign inputs, but separation alone does not establish what a risk score means or when it should be trusted. We introduce Counterfactual Neighborhood Risk Fields (CNRF), an evidence-grounded framework for selective VLM safety. CNRF constructs context-matched benign-harmful counterfactual pairs, uses their representation differences as capability-related risk directions, and estimates neighborhood support separately from risk. This separation prevents unfamiliarity from being conflated with harmfulness and enables selective intervention rather than blanket rejection. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20681v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Formal inequality proving requires mathematical reasoning and exact computation, often connected through intermediate lemmas and goal reformulations. We introduce IneqAgent, an agentic framework combining LLM reasoning with symbolic computation for inequality proving in Lean4. Lemma-level Monte Carlo Tree Search coordinates lemma construction, goal reformulation, and symbolic backend selection. Complementary sum-of-squares, Bernstein, and successive difference-substitution backends produce exact certificates for local Lean proof generation. The agent integrates these proofs with LLM-generated steps and uses Lean feedback to construct complete proofs checked against the original theorem statements. On four benchmarks, IneqAgent with DeepSeek-V4-Flash solves 175 of 186 problems (94.09%), achieving the highest overall success rate among the evaluated methods. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20685v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Symbolic regression searches for an equation that explains observed data. Numerical error is commonly used to guide the search, but it alone can favor an accurate surrogate over a candidate with the right structure. We propose L2G-SR, a framework for LLM-based symbolic regression that guides search with a learned structural verifier. We construct structural supervision signal using tree edit distance (TED), accounting for commutative operators and alternative expression forms. A verifier first aligns numerical observations with the formulas, then learns to score a candidate's structural similarity to the target formula. At search time, the target formula is hidden and the verifier complements numerical error in parent selection. An analyst then uses verifier feedback and diagnostic tools to propose revisions, which a generator converts into refined expressions. Abstract: This paper challenges the understanding capabilities of existing AI paradigms and emerging world models by asking a fundamental question: How quickly can reality change before an intelligent system can no longer reliably perceive, reason, and act? Abstract: In LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS), a local mistake can propagate as other agents build on it, turning a correctable error into a failed task. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20782v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The closed world asks AI for specialized competence and lets it manufacture the iid data its theory assumes: a fixed criterion licenses collecting examples until the task is covered. The open world asks for versatility --- taking up tasks a machine was not built for, from few examples and with little prior from a human designer --- and offers data that is grouped, not shuffled. Its tasks are not known in advance, so a machine must do inference-time learning (1st requirement). Modeling tasks as sharing latent factors and decomposing the training objective, we derive two more: a *rich representation*, retaining more than iid generalization requires, and a predictive disentanglement that aligns inputs and outputs into matched low-dimensional groups. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20786v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-modal agents have made significant progress in interacting with open worlds. However, their ability to self-evolve remains limited. Supervised fine-tuning enables imitation but not active experience organization, while outcome-based reinforcement learning promotes exploration yet underuses intermediate trajectory information. Therefore, we propose EvolvingBrain, which uses an adaptive skill system as the brain for agent self-evolution, consisting of two following components. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20805v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A reasoning trace retained at answer time plays two roles: it can raise accuracy, and it can compete with the current evidence when the two disagree. We disentangle these roles by crossing verified evidence versions with the traces generated from each and answering from the same traces and evidence under two configurations: continuation of the model's own thinking and a separate answer call. Across three model families (gpt-oss, Gemma4, Qwen3) on HotpotQA and MuSiQue, the separate call raises evidence-following over continuation by 29.9 to 60.6 points. On the same pairs, removing the trace lowers accuracy by similar amounts under both configurations. Abstract: We present a general declarative framework for anticipatory reasoning about interactive motion in complex dynamic environments. Our focus is on (explainable) anticipatory space-time mental model formation at a semantic level to heuristically guide low-level motion computation. Our method is hybrid, modular and elaboration tolerant integrating: 1) An ASP model characterising the dynamics of interactive motion trajectories; 2) Semantically-guided prediction for deriving `branching trajectory futures'; and 3) An energy-based {optimisation} model to evaluate, rank and filter anticipations. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20921v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Most debate about releasing capable AI systems treats the choice as binary: keep the model behind an API, or publish the weights. That framing runs together two separate decisions. One is how capable a system may become. The other is who may obtain a given capability, and on what terms. This paper is about the second decision. We propose a Multi-Tiered AI Accessibility Model (MAIAM) that sorts access by purpose, safety, and capability instead of by release artifact. Tier 1, AI for Learning, is broadly accessible and deliberately capability-bounded. Tier 2, AI for Exploration, serves research and development under registration, identity, and usage controls that tighten as capability rises. Abstract: Compositional structure is pervasive in nature and across scales: atoms combine into molecules, molecules into cells, and cells into organisms, while further compositional hierarchies appear within each level. More broadly, compositionality, the reuse and recombination of parts into novel structures, is a fundamental source of interesting complexity in both natural and artificial systems. Here, we fill this gap by formalizing a simple idea: compositional structure emerges when parts, considered together, reveal shared structure that is not captured when those parts are modeled separately. Abstract: Research on deceptive alignment is becoming increasingly urgent as frontier-model capabilities advance and their risk of causing catastrophic harm increases. Alignment faking is a form of deceptive alignment, with the compliance gap serving as a key behavioural indicator. This behaviour remains understudied in small LLMs and prior mechanistic interventions have not been shown to mitigate the compliance gap. We use a novel bag-of-words feature elicitation pipeline for SAE steering to identify what we construe as concept-level steering directions. Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is credited with gains beyond the domain its rewards check, such as higher MMLU accuracy after training on mathematics. Such accuracies are usually read out of the model's text by an answer extractor. A model that learns to write its answer where the extractor looks can therefore score higher without answering better. We measure how much of the gain reported by extractors copied from public code arises this way. We generate outputs from a base model and its RL model and score them twice: with those extractors, and with one extractor of our own that reads a stated answer whether it is in the answer box \boxed{} or in the text. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20640v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Global streamflow forecasting supports flood preparedness, yet data-driven models trained on reanalysis lose skill when driven by operational forecasts, increasingly so with lead time. AIFL addresses this shift with a two-stage transfer-learning recipe and a deterministic LSTM, but it feeds one forecast lead time into the whole input window and gives no uncertainty. We ask how far this open recipe can be extended without changing its recurrent core. KNOU-Flood keeps a single-layer LSTM and the two-stage training and changes the information around it: a longer input window (424 days), lead-aware forecast inputs, GraphCast as a second forecast source next to ECMWF HRES, and a latent-noise ensemble trained with the fair CRPS. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20680v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are typically trained on hundreds of millions to billions of activation tokens, yet little work has tested whether this scale is necessary. We study how much activation data SAEs need by training four SAE architectures on three language models with budgets ranging from 5M tokens to a 500M-token reference. We measure two notions of convergence: functional behavior on standard evaluations and one-to-one reproducibility of learned features. Functional data requirements are strongly metric-dependent: reconstruction often approaches the full-data reference at substantially smaller budgets, whereas feature reproducibility continues to improve with data. Abstract: We introduce TurboMamba, a language-model architecture for faster inference, faster training, and better token prediction. A global Mamba-3 model runs once per completed token block. A small Transformer uses this global context and earlier tokens within the block to predict the next token. Three lightweight additions improve local predictions: direct access to the previous block's last token, a small correction to next-token scores, and a learned mixture with recent-token frequencies. We compare twelve small-scale implementations on public FineWeb-Edu, with comparable parameter counts and shared training-budget caps. The baselines include Transformer, Mamba-3, Jamba, and Zamba. The Jamba and Zamba versions use Mamba-3 in place of their original Mamba modules. TurboMamba achieves the lowest mean test prediction loss (negative log-likelihood, NLL) among all twelve models. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20686v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-head latent attention (MLA) compresses the content of a key-value cache into a shared latent per token, making low-bit storage attractive for long-context inference. At two bits, errors in this representation perturb both attention matching and value readout, with effects that depend on error direction and reconstruction scale. We introduce RoLaQ (Rotation-calibrated Latent Quantization), an offline method for joint rotation and range calibration. RoLaQ refines a shared rotation within subspaces defined by the frozen key and value projections, and jointly learns quantization ranges whose thresholds and reconstruction gains are coupled to control the shared signal's response. Prediction matching and attention-output supervision guide calibration with model weights frozen. articles.title: On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20687v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Residual context is key to unlocking the speed-quality Pareto frontier of diffusion language models (DLMs) by carrying forward predictive distributions across denoising steps. Yet turning this seemingly simple mechanism into an effective learning paradigm is far from simple: there is no clear recipe for how residual context should be learned. We introduce ORL, a framework for on-policy residual learning in DLMs. Algorithmically, we identify that residual learning is inherently on-policy. ORL learns from model-induced residual trajectories on the fly and introduces an entropy-contraction objective that sharpens predictions as the model revisits its own predictions. System-wise, exact residual supervision requires capturing, retaining, and reprocessing many trajectory-dependent states. articles.title: Quantile-Guided Diffusion for Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20739v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quantile forecasts summarize uncertainty at each future time step, while diffusion forecasters represent it through sampled future trajectories. We study how predicted quantiles can serve as distributional controls for diffusion forecasting. Specifically, we investigate how the mechanism of quantile integration affects its effectiveness in guiding a pretrained diffusion forecaster. We find that residual control throughout the denoising network yields the most consistent improvements. We instantiate this approach as Control-TS, which learns a quantile-control pathway while keeping the pretrained backbone frozen. Across eight benchmarks, Control-TS consistently improves the backbone's CRPS, achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art forecasting models, and retains its gains in capacity-matched comparisons. Abstract: Many modern learning problems require comparing probability distributions whose individual observations are themselves probability measures, naturally giving rise to meta-measures in $\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{P}(\Omega))$. Abstract: Mechanistic interpretability aims to uncover how neural networks use their parameters to implement their impressive neural algorithms. Although previous work has uncovered substantial structure in the intermediate representations that networks use, little progress has been made to understand how the parameters and nonlinearities of networks perform computations on those representations. In this work, we present a method that brings us closer to this understanding by decomposing a language model's parameters into subcomponents that each implement only a small part of the model's learned algorithm, while simultaneously requiring only a small fraction of those subcomponents to account for the network's behavior on any input. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) trained on vast amounts of data have demonstrated impressive performance over a range of tasks, but future performance gains will require increasing amounts of data and compute. Federated Learning (FL) facilitates training on decentralized private data, but client resource limitations can make training impractical, particularly as model sizes continue to expand. These resource constraints make the assumption of a shared server-client architecture impractical. Model heterogeneous FL offers a promising alternative by adapting model size to client capabilities; however, previous work is limited to the pre-training setting, and conclusions on sub-network selection do not necessarily hold for fine-tuning. Abstract: Imagined speech decoding from EEG offers a promising route toward naturalistic brain-computer interfaces. Traditional closed-set classifiers treat semantic categories as independent labels and do not explicitly exploit relationships among linguistic intents, limiting output flexibility. We adapt a multimodal contrastive learning framework to imagined speech, aligning EEG trials with language representations in the embedding space of a frozen pretrained text encoder. An EEG encoder is trained with a composite objective combining semantically reweighted EEG-sentence alignment and text-prototype-based class discrimination, encouraging semantic structure while preserving separability among 39 intent categories. Abstract: Understanding why listeners enjoy music is difficult because the experience is subjective and changes as a piece unfolds. Electroencephalography (EEG) offers a non-invasive way to study neural responses during listening, yet earlier work has mostly treated music emotion as a categorical label or relied on black-box models. We formulate enjoyment prediction as a regression problem on the public MUSIN-G dataset, which contains 128-channel EEG from 20 listeners together with song-level enjoyment ratings. Six deep learning models were compared under a participant-wise protocol, in which 15 listeners were used for training and validation and 5 were held out for testing. Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) based on large language models (LLMs) have become a powerful way to address complex problems, and their effectiveness depends critically on the collaboration topology that decides which agents participate and how they communicate. Recent work learns to generate this topology from the task query, fitting the generator to corpora of execution-verified graphs. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20634v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation asks one question at volume: does this evidence support this claim? The answer is one bit, yet most pipelines obtain it from a text generator and pay generation prices for the prose wrapped around it. We compare a non-generative decision model, which returns a typed value from a declared enumeration together with a native probability and no text, against a frontier LLM configured as an engineer would deploy it for binary classification. Both answer the same 495 human-labelled claims from LLM-AggreFact, so every comparison is within-item. We report three things. First, the two systems are statistically indistinguishable on the metric this task is conventionally scored by, a paired difference of -0.56 points, Jev minus Astra, at a 187-fold cost difference. articles.title: Exploring the Design Space of Permutation Diffusion LLMs
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20635v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Permutation generation with language models requires both text-conditioned ranking and a global one-to-one assignment between candidates and output positions. We study this problem through three diffusion-LLM parameterizations: hard-assignment prediction over shuffled candidate-index sequences, soft-assignment prediction over doubly stochastic matrices, and direct ordering-score prediction followed by sorting. The three families place permutation constraints at different stages of prediction and decoding and therefore support different training objectives and sampling procedures. We evaluate these designs on recommendation reranking across three Amazon domains with candidate sets of size 10 and 20. articles.title: AbridgeKV: Compressing Long Reasoning into the KV Cache of Learned Pause Tokens
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20641v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long chain-of-thought decoding is memory-bound: the KV cache of the generated tokens grows linearly with the test-time compute being spent. Evicting cache entries does not fix this, because a model never trained on a cache with entries removed generates longer, often up to the length limit. We instead train the model to compress its own output. AbridgeKV compresses each completed block of generated text into the KV entries of a few learned pause tokens. These are extra input tokens with trained embeddings that produce no output. Once the pause tokens have encoded the block, AbridgeKV frees the block's original cache; subsequent tokens attend to the pause tokens' KV entries in its place. articles.title: CoTS: Competitive Token Selection for Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20642v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent latent reasoning methods move beyond discrete Chain-of-Thought (CoT) by replacing sampled tokens with continuous soft embeddings or hidden states, enabling richer intermediate representations and preserving alternative reasoning paths. However, the need for latent reasoning varies across decoding steps: confident predictions favor discrete commitment, whereas ambiguous steps benefit from preserving multiple plausible alternatives. Existing approaches typically handle this variation through either global soft activation or hard switching based on uncertainty thresholds, treating latent intervention as an all-or-nothing decision rather than continuously adapting its strength. articles.title: Does Personalization Break Trust? Open-Set Rejection Calibration Under Few-Shot On-Device Intent Adaptation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20652v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Always-on virtual assistants increasingly personalize on-device to new user-specific commands via few-shot fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA), but this adaptation is evaluated almost exclusively on whether it learns the new commands, not on whether the assistant can still recognize an input that matches none of its intents - the out-of-scope (OOS) rejection problem. We show that naive few-shot LoRA personalization degrades OOS-rejection AUROC (area under the ROC curve) on every one of five public intent-classification benchmarks (mean drop $0.055$--$0.258$, five seeds each), while in-scope accuracy is preserved. A scorer-invariant check shows part of this drop is an artifact of the standard confidence scorer's own miscalibration under adaptation, though a smaller, genuine effect remains under any scorer; we trace it to a measurable shrinkage of the embedding margin around known-intent regions (pooled Spearman rho=0.61$). articles.title: Reference-Guided Turn-Taking Style Transfer for Full-Duplex Spoken Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20763v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Full-duplex spoken language models decide at every frame whether to take the floor, defining a conversational personality -- yet each set of weights encodes exactly one, which human speakers bracket rather than share. Existing controls mostly act from outside; none identifies the quantity that sets how much the model speaks. We identify it: a single late-layer residual-stream direction, the initiative vector, extracted from the model's own conversations without training or annotation. The same direction reads the decision, anticipating onsets up to 800 ms ahead, and shifts it: scaled during generation, it moves speech ratio from 6-12% to 42-61% (no steering: 21-30%), consistently across conversations, weights, and corpora. articles.title: Verdict: Encode Once, Decide Many
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20778v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automating organizational work means answering many small typed questions about one piece of state (does this email need a reply, how urgent is it, who owns it) with probabilities good enough to act on without a human. The open typed-decision model we compare against, like a standard cross-encoder, answers each question with a separate pass over the input. We present Verdict-MQ, an open encoder that reads a case once and answers all of its questions: given identical retained state tokens after truncation (verified on every reported case), a structured attention mask makes the state encoding independent of the questions, keeps questions from influencing each other, and makes option order irrelevant by construction. articles.title: APRiL: An Open-ended Benchmark for Chinese Social Awareness in Large Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20785v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used in social interactions, where appropriate responses require recognizing implicit cues, inferring mental states, identifying conflicts, and considering potential consequences. However, existing benchmarks often focus on specific social abilities, constrained task formats, or particular interaction settings, offering limited coverage of social awareness across diverse contexts. To address this gap, we introduce APRiL, an open-ended benchmark for Chinese social awareness with instance-specific rubrics. APRiL contains 2,196 Social Awareness Evaluation Instances across six categories and two complementary tasks: Social Scenario Analysis evaluates models' understanding of social cues, mental states, and conflict structures, while Socially Aware Response assesses whether they can translate this understanding into appropriate, natural responses. articles.title: PRISM: Transfer and Limits of Activation Interventions in Tool-Calling Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20808v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent literature shows that unsafe tool calls can often accompany textual refusals in language models. To investigate this hidden vulnerability, we introduce PRISM, a framework for evaluating the transfer of activation interventions across precision, languages, and scales. Our findings demonstrate that leveraging lower-resource settings (specifically quantized NF4 labels and cross-lingual transfer) offers a robust pathway to expose and improve model alignment. Notably, using behavioral labels from an NF4 copy enables stable intervention estimation even with very few scenarios. Furthermore, these alignment improvements transfer effectively across languages: five-language NF4-supervised directions successfully transfer to held-out Arabic, reducing unsafe violations in Llama-3.1-8B by 21.95 percentage points without target-language tuning. articles.title: Wolof-Adapted Industry-Ready Open-Weight Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20824v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Wolof is spoken by 23M people, mostly in Senegal, but remains weakly supported by open-weight language models, while API models raise cost, governance, and sovereignty constraints for local deployments. In this paper, we present 0.6B-14B open-weight models adapted to Wolof through instruction tuning, preference alignment, and model merging. After presenting the pipeline and data, extensive experiments on 63~public and in-house tasks show good performance on Wolof understanding and generation while remaining effective on other languages and cross-lingual skills, with the 8B and 14B models being particularly competitive with substantially larger commercial systems. The models are currently being evaluated in internal customer-care pilots and are publicly available at https://huggingface.co/collections/Orange/wolof-lm .

articles.title: CoTranslator: Reverse to Forward Chain-of-Thought Translator for Reasoning Distillation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20828v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reasoning distillation requires chain-of-thought (CoT) data with correct answers, but obtaining such data efficiently remains challenging. Forward CoT generation (FCG) followed by rejection sampling (RS) produces verified, question-only responses, yet may require many teacher calls for difficult problems. Reverse CoT generation (RCG) is cheaper because it conditions on the known answer, but access to this answer can lead to post-hoc rationalization and a mismatch with the student's answer-free inference setting. We propose CoTranslator, which learns to translate reverse CoT responses toward the distribution of verified forward responses. Trained on a small set of paired reverse and rejection-sampled forward responses, it supports large-scale generation and verification of student training data. Across six student models evaluated on six mathematics benchmarks, CoTranslator improves average accuracy over semantic suppression by up to $5.8

articles.title: PEDBench: Can Speech Models Detect Phonetic Errors?
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20830v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Phonetic error detection (PED) aims to identify phoneme-level substitutions, deletions, and insertions and is essential for educational and clinical speech assessment and intervention. Despite recent advances in speech models for phoneme recognition, their ability to reliably detect fine-grained phonetic errors remains unclear because of a lack of high-quality evaluation data. To address this gap, we introduce PEDBench, the first PED benchmark spanning a continuum from natural to controlled speech. It comprises real-world recordings of spoken errors made by children (N=334), scripted error productions by human actors (N=1,188), and synthetic error productions generated using phone-conditioned text-to-speech (N=1,083). All phonetic annotations were transcribed and verified by two phonetically trained annotators. articles.title: Does Morphological Correctness Matter for Tokenization? A Scrambled Control Study in Tagalog
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20859v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Typology-aware tokenizers are motivated by the claim that segmentation which respects morpheme boundaries preserves information that frequency-driven segmentation destroys. Studies routinely establish that it helps while assuming the boundaries must be linguistically correct. We separate them. Tagalog marks voice with infixes (s-um-ulat 'wrote', s-in-ulat 'was written'), so the root is not contiguous and no sequence of BPE merges can recover it. We build MorphAustro-Tok, a tokenizer that emits the root as a contiguous unit followed by a positional infix token, and compare it against a corpus-matched BPE baseline and, at two of three fertility levels, against a scrambled-morpheme control that preserves morph count, invertibility and per-type consistency while randomising the pseudo-infix. articles.title: Prune the Summary, Not the History: Source-Judged Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20927v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents rely on context compaction: when the interaction history outgrows the context window, a compressor replaces it with a natural-language summary. We show that these summaries contain more than a record of what happened. Compaction prompts ask for decisions and next steps, so each summary mixes facts established by the environment with reasoning written by the compressor, and the agent cannot tell the two apart afterwards. In an analysis of a widely used structured compressor, 83% of failed runs trace back to an action that carries out a specific summary entry, most of which no environment output supports. We propose Source-Judged Compaction (SJC), a training-free post-processing step that scores each summary entry for whether it has a source in the environment outputs or the previous summary, and removes the entries that do not. articles.title: BD-HazardVLM: Probing Vision-Language Models for Latent Defensive-Driving Hazards in Bangladesh Road Scenes
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20627v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-language models are increasingly used for driving-scene understanding, yet their defensive reasoning under weakly structured Global South traffic remains unclear. We introduce BD-HazardVLM, a diagnostic benchmark of 500 Bangladesh road-scene images, comprising 375 from RSUD20K and 125 from TFP-BD, annotated for hazard presence, primary hazard category, risk timing, severity, defensive actions, visible evidence, and hallucination- and Western-road-bias traps. We evaluate Qwen2.5-VL-7B, InternVL3-8B, and MiniCPM-V-4.6 using a shared zero-shot task definition and structured output schema. Binary hazard-presence accuracy ranges from 88.0 percent to 89.2 percent, essentially matching the 89.0 percent majority-class baseline. Fine-grained reasoning is substantially weaker: category accuracy remains below 40 percent, risk-timing accuracy ranges from 1.6 percent to 12.4 percent, and exact defensive-action matching remains below 2 percent.

articles.title: Towards automatic digital garment assembly
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20651v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Creating digital garments from existing two-dimensional patterns remains a time-consuming process. Although patterns are widely available in digital form, their assembly in garment CAD software involves manual definition of sewing operations and arrangement of the pattern panels for drape simulation. We present two learning-based approaches that automate both tasks using the 2D vector pattern as their sole input. Our automatic sewing model operates at the segment level, leveraging a Transformer encoder with multiple prediction heads. Our novel architecture supports many-to-many, ordered segment correspondences, as well as hems, overlapping seams needed for multilayer garments, and construction properties such as seam allowances and stitch types, required for the finished virtual garment but neglected by previous methods. articles.title: Orbia: Do Generated Videos Form a Consistent 3D World?
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20693v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Video generators serve as interactive worlds for exploration and simulation, yet realistic and visually appealing frames do not necessarily depict a consistent 3D world. Existing benchmarks assess selected geometric properties or use vision-language models to judge memory and consistency, leaving systematic 3D evaluation underexplored. We introduce Orbia, the first benchmark dedicated to a systematic and comprehensive evaluation of 3D consistency in interactive world models. Through controlled exploration and revisit, we organize the evaluation into three dimensions: input preservation, generated-content persistence, and 3D self-consistency. For input preservation, registered RGB-D references and annotated anchors support appearance, geometry, and spatial stability measurements. articles.title: WorldCast: Exploring Intelligent Visual Generation in World State Prediction
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20731v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humans interpret multimodal observations of the world and forecast how it will evolve. Recent multimodal generative systems have demonstrated similar capabilities: they can integrate multimodal context and synthesize visual outputs that depict changes in the world. To characterize this emerging trajectory, we organize model capabilities into a four-level hierarchy and discover that higher-level tasks remain relatively underexplored despite model progress. To bridge this gap, we explore model performance on multi-step world state prediction, a high-level task that requires models to forecast successive future world states from multimodal observations and diverse references. Such a task requires models to possess entangled understanding and generation capabilities, as well as extensive world knowledge to translate human action sequences, physical transformations, and abstract visual reasoning into coherent visual outputs. articles.title: Purify Before You Align: Improving Representation Alignment for Diffusion Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20761v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Representation alignment improves and accelerates diffusion training by encouraging intermediate features to match a pretrained visual encoder. However, standard alignment matches pretrained representations without distinguishing what information may be more useful for generation. We introduce local appearance purification (LAP), which improves generation quality and makes encoders such as MAE more effective alignment targets by removing locally predictable content and aligning to the residual. LAP modifies only the alignment target, and requires no changes to diffusion training or inference. Through controlled interventions within a fixed encoder, we show that effective alignment depends on what information the target emphasizes, not simply how much image information it contains. articles.title: ReasonUni: Reasoning-Augmented Reconstruction Advances Unified Multimodal Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20781v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Image-to-text (I2T) understanding and text-to-image (T2I) generation are dual tasks in unified multimodal models (UMMs). Reconstructive post-training couples these tasks, but existing reconstruction-based methods remain perception-centric and provide limited supervision for reasoning about structure, intent, and transformation. We propose ReasonUni, a reasoning-augmented reconstructive post-training framework that extends this coupling beyond perception. Given an original image and an editing instruction, the UMM first reasons about what and how to edit and describes the target state, then generates the corresponding target image conditioned on this understanding output. To jointly optimize both modules, we introduce TreeGRPO, a tree-structured reinforcement learning method that samples multiple reasoning paths and candidate images per path, then aggregates visual rewards to update both modules under a unified objective. articles.title: Blame Errant Words, Not the Canvas: Defect-Aware Spatial Credit Assignment for Visual Text Generation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20794v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent reinforcement learning approaches have improved visual text generation, yet generated images still suffer from incorrect wording and malformed glyphs. We identify two coupled limitations: recognition-based rewards often overlook visible glyph defects, while whole-image scalar feedback obscures the uneven quality of individual text regions. These limitations motivate our central principle: $\textit{Blame errant words, not the canvas}$, to effectively preserve local quality distinctions. Building on TextDART, we propose $\mathbf{SCANNER}$, which turns these regional judgments into spatially differentiated policy feedback. Abstract: Generative gameplay requires more than immediate responses to player actions.Actions should have persistent consequences, while the generated world should act according to its own state and rules, shaping the player's situation and subsequent choices. Video generation captures local dynamics, but limited history, partially observed game state, and the need for contextual behavior decisions make such interactions difficult to sustain through audiovisual prediction alone. We introduce \rig (Reciprocally Interactive Generation), a framework for reciprocal interaction in generative gameplay. \rig combines persistent state and configurable rules, contextual interaction reasoning, and action-conditioned audiovisual generation. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20818v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Unified multimodal generation covers discrete, continuous, and hybrid paradigms. Discrete approaches with single-codebook visual tokenizers align naturally with text modeling but have limited representational capacity. Continuous and hybrid approaches retain richer visual representations, but they model text and images in heterogeneous spaces with different training objectives, potentially introducing optimization conflicts between modalities with misaligned representation spaces. These choices expose a central question: how to efficiently model high-capacity visual representations alongside textual content in a shared optimization space within a single backbone. articles.title: MARS - A foundational map auto-regressor
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20843v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Map generation tasks feature extensive non-structural vectorized data (e.g., points, polylines, and polygons) and thus pose significant challenges to common pixel-wise generative models. Conventional approaches use multiple stages, first segmenting these features at the pixel level and then performing vectorized post-processing, with errors and complexity compounding at each stage. Motivated by the recent success of auto-regressive language modeling, we propose the first map foundation model, named Map Auto-Regressor (MARS), that is capable of generating both multi-polyline road networks and polygon buildings in a unified manner. For training MARS, we collected to our knowledge the largest multi-class map extraction dataset totaling 3.4M examples, which we call MAP-3M. articles.title: Probing Negation Understanding in Vision-Language Models With Object Attention
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20852v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Negation is a fundamental aspect of language understanding and it is important vision-language models (VLMs) are able to process it effectively. We investigate how VLMs process negation by analysing attention patterns of different models. We draw comparisons between human gaze and attention in models when processing affirmative vs negated statements. We compare object level model attention to human eye-fixations in both binary and multary settings, evaluating with both synthetic and realistic datasets. We find models generally do not follow human-like attention patterns when resolving negation, suggesting they rely on mechanisms outside of attention. While layerwise analysis shows that PaliGemma2-3B shifts object attention to the alternative under negation, our headwise ablations suggest this is a byproduct rather than a negation processing mechanism. articles.title: DefoliationCAM: An Edge-AI System for Real-Time Insect Defoliation Severity Assessment in Grapevines
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20879v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Insect-induced defoliation threatens grapevine health and yield, yet severity assessment relies on subjective manual scouting. We developed DefoliationCAM (D-CAM), a solar-powered edge AI system that estimates canopy defoliation and transmits results via LoRa to a web dashboard. The pipeline uses YOLOX-Nano to localize grapevine cordons in 4K images and a MobileNet-based classifier with lightweight channel attention to classify 320 x 320 pixel patches. Abstract: While foundation models and vision transformers (ViTs) have redefined visual representations, current active learning (AL) strategies for these backbones largely operate at the patch or region level, where annotation requirements remain high due to extensive pixel labeling. We introduce TEAL (Token-space Efficient Active Learning), the first pixel-level AL framework built around ViT representations. TEAL uses a frozen ViT backbone and performs diversity-based selection directly on its native token lattice, avoiding the artifacts introduced by interpolating token embeddings to dense pixel resolutions. arXiv:2610.20917v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Occupancy predictors rely on large persistent banks of Gaussians or learned queries whose size is fixed by hand. Common pruning proxies, such as opacity, activation frequency, or parameter magnitude, do not measure whether removing a row changes the model's voxel decisions. We introduce Decision-FLIP, a budget-free compilation framework whose scoring and structure selection need only unlabeled calibration inputs. Exact Mean-FLIP scores each persistent row by the number of voxel argmax decisions that change when the row is removed from the readout; a guarded Otsu split of the log-score distribution selects the survivor count without a target and abstains when the split is unsupported; and the survivors are physically compiled into a smaller checkpoint, so camera sampling, attention, and aggregation shrink with the bank. articles.title: VELD-QA: A Large-Scale Dataset for Visual Evidence Grounding and Question Answering in Long Documents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20964v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Existing long-document QA benchmarks rarely combine large-scale human-authored questions with detailed visual evidence annotations, limiting diagnosis of evidence localization and interpretation failures. We present VELD-QA, a large-scale benchmark for Visual Evidence grounding and question answering in Long Documents. It contains 15,000 fully human-authored question-answer pairs across 5,859 real-world PDFs totaling 372,445 pages, balancing chart, table, and complex-layout tasks. Human annotations identify supporting pages and evidence elements and describe cited visual content, enabling separate retrieval and interpretation evaluation. We evaluate nine vision-language models under four evidence settings and seven retrieval-augmented and agentic systems. Our analysis identifies bottlenecks in evidence localization and interpretation. Retrieval-based methods substantially underperform the oracle setting with ground-truth supporting pages

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20973v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Geo-foundation models (GFMs) are typically evaluated by downstream task predictive performance, revealing little about which physical features they are sensitive to or use in prediction. This limits developers' ability to test hypotheses about model behaviour and users' ability to select models for new tasks. We propose Physics-Informed Concept Probing (PiCo), a post-hoc framework for explaining GFM predictions. PiCo identifies concept vectors in a GFM's embedding space by generating synthetic multispectral satellite observations from a 3D radiative transfer model coupled with a game engine. These vectors reveal physical sensitivities that inform domain-based hypotheses about downstream performance. arXiv:2610.20990v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spatial agents have access to reconstruction and segmentation tools, yet inconsistent predictions and fragmented object identities can prevent their outputs from becoming reliable 3D scene information. A simple oracle experiment exposes this perception bottleneck: replacing tool-predicted perception with ground-truth 3D bounding boxes raises an agent to nearly full score across five object-centric VSI-Bench tasks, while retaining the same reasoning tools. Abstract: Diffusion models are notoriously expensive to train, requiring large-scale datasets to learn how to gradually reverse the noise from images over multiple small denoising steps. Current approaches focus on distilling the number of diffusion steps, neglecting potential redundancies of the training data. In this paper, we explore the potential of harnessing eigensamples to train diffusion models on significantly smaller datasets, while preserving model performance. To mitigate the sensitivity to affine transformations of eigenimages, we harness the latent space of a pre-trained CLIP model. We next compute latent eigenvectors by performing principal component analysis (PCA) in CLIP space. Abstract: Data selection reallocates training support across visual concepts, including objects, attributes, color, texture, and backgrounds. Different allocation strategies may produce varied downstream model behavior, especially for tail concepts supported by only a few samples. Discarding them can hurt test-time robustness, while overemphasizing samples lying on category boundaries may introduce unstable training signals. This work explicitly investigates this relationship across fine-grained, spurious-correlation, and general image classification, as well as multimodal pretraining. Specifically, we use sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to extract concept activations from individual images. During selection, we accumulate the dataset-level concept support for each added sample. Abstract: Identifying individual dogs from barks in real-world videos remains challenging and largely unexplored. Solving this problem would enable long-term behavioral analysis, veterinary monitoring, and animal welfare monitoring by attributing vocalizations and behaviors to the correct individual. Real-world videos are challenging because multiple dogs may bark simultaneously, become occluded, or move in and out of view. Prior studies show that canine vocalizations and visual appearance contain discriminative identity information, but these modalities have largely been studied independently. Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are a promising approach to general purpose robot manipulation. While the internal computation of vision-language models, which compose the backbone of VLAs, has been studied extensively, less is known about how their perceptual and semantic representations are transformed into action in VLA models. We study this question mechanistically in three frontier VLA models ($\pi_{0.5}$, MolmoAct2, and MolmoBot) by analyzing the causal pathways through which the input image and the instruction shape actions. Across the three models, activation patching shows that causally relevant information influences the action expert (AE) through a narrow band of mid-to-late cross-attention layers, which we term the action-conditioning interface. Abstract: Can better feature discovery improve control over robot behavior through internal interventions and training data? We investigate whether recovering this structure provides an interpretable interface for steering vision-language-action models and shaping the data from which they learn. We show that BSFs recover several multi-dimensional task-relevant features underlying the model's computation (e.g., perception, language, proprioceptive state, episode phase, and control variables). Abstract: Reliable absolute heading estimation is critical for road-vehicle navigation, particularly when magnetic, inertial, or GNSS-based references are degraded. This paper presents a skylight polarization navigation method that estimates vehicle heading by globally optimizing a Rayleigh sky model against measurements from a division-of-focal-plane polarimetric camera. The proposed framework combines a pinhole camera model, a single-scattering Rayleigh polarization model, and a solar position algorithm to synthesize the expected full image angle of polarization distribution for candidate vehicle states. Abstract: A mesh of interceptors defending a fixed site must spread over the predicted arrival point of an approaching object. This is a recurring task in multi-agent robotics: N agents, each covering a disc of radius r, spread over a probability density so that a point drawn from it falls within some agent's disc. We give closed forms for the quantities that bound performance before any policy is chosen, and validate each by Monte Carlo. Abstract: Damage-recovery algorithms often rank gaits from short trials, yet a gait that performs well briefly may not remain effective during continued execution. In reset-free recovery, each trial also changes the physical state inherited by the next. We introduce persistent profile-guided reset-free recovery (PGRR), which predicts multiple outcomes over repeated gait execution and uses conservative uncertainty-aware estimates to guide short online probes without resetting the robot. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20840v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Robotic manipulation is inherently geometric, but what shape does the world take inside the policy that performs it? Prior work on vision-language-action (VLA) policies establishes that task-relevant variables are linearly readable from activations, yet readability certifies only that a variable is present and says nothing about the shape its values trace, which may be curved and multi-dimensional. Using controlled sweeps, natural rollouts, linear probes, and activation interventions, we build a taxonomy of seven task-relevant concepts in VLA models. We find that realized geometry is predominantly multi-dimensional and is shaped by the constraints under which the policy acts. In particular, the methodology introduced in this work addresses the use of sustainably powered autonomous surface vessels (ASVs) to perform scientific missions that prioritize locations of maximum interest. Because these locations of maximum interest are not known a priori but are rather identified based on in-situ measurements, online adaptation is essential for mission planning. Abstract: Vehicles that lose control at the handling limit through icing, hydroplaning, or an abrupt evasive maneuver fall outside the operating envelope of production safety systems such as electronic stability control, which focus on preventing instability rather than recovering from it. Expert drivers regain authority in these conditions by drifting. Existing autonomous recovery approaches are validated on idealized scenarios, define "recovered" states empirically and inconsistently, or rely on offline-planned trajectories rather than acting online. We address these gaps by first training a racing policy with reinforcement learning that learns drifting as a time-optimal maneuver, then adapting it to recovery through continued training with a minimum-time reward. arXiv:2610.20875v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sustainably powered mobile robots enable long-duration observational missions by harvesting energy from the environment. However, effective autonomy requires the robots to make decisions as to how to allocate this energy to maximize information quality over time. In this paper, we study a persistent (infinite-horizon) speed trajectory optimization problem that is posed as a periodic optimal control problem in which a robot repeatedly traverses a fixed closed path, coupling a super-linear propulsion cost with dynamic information gain and decay. Using the information-theoretic quantity of clarity as an information metric, we first derive the necessary conditions for optimal control. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20895v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Satisfying safety constraints for systems with second-order dynamics is challenging because a position constraint may require infeasible deceleration. Higher-order control barrier functions (CBFs) provide an approach for expressing safety conditions for such systems but feasibility depends on the system dynamics and available control authority. We develop a constructive approach for designing feasible safety constraints for second-order control-affine systems. Starting from a signed distance function (SDF), we construct collision-free spheres, i.e., bubbles, in position space, and use their quadratic geometry and overlap to construct a velocity-dependent safety constraint. The associated safe set is represented as a union of intersections and enforced through a quadratic-program safety filter. Abstract: Task-Oriented Grasping (TOG) has emerged as an important skill for purposeful robotic manipulation. Given the task of using a knife to "slice bread," a robot must choose to grasp from the handle, whereas for "hand[ing] the knife over," it is preferable for the handle to remain unobstructed for safe handoff. Current approaches for TOG either focus on 2D planar grasping, remain limited by their reliance on task-agnostic grasp generators, or are constrained by reliance on finite, manually-annotated, task-specific grasp datasets that cannot cover all possible grasp-task pairs. To that end, we present TGrasp6D, a vision-language based approach for generating task-oriented 6DoF grasps in a zero-shot manner. Abstract: Robust adaptive control is vital for keeping robots safe while actively reducing uncertainty in unfamiliar settings. However, traditional methods are often conservative since they fail to account for guaranteed future parameter learning during planning and struggle to scale to high-dimensional systems. In this work, we present A-SLS, a learning-aware robust adaptive model predictive control (RAMPC) framework based on system-level synthesis. A-SLS forecasts future parameter uncertainty and preserves correlations between process disturbances, parameter error, and estimate updates to construct tight, guaranteed reachable sets that account for future information gain. We also develop a GPU-accelerated A-SLS solver to enable real-time performance. Abstract: Generating dynamically feasible motions for legged and manipulating robots requires solving a large, nonlinear, non-convex optimal control problem (OCP) in which contact wrenches must satisfy friction-cone constraints throughout the motion, not only at isolated instants. Existing solvers are sensitive to the initial guess and scale poorly with the number of joints. This paper introduces LEAP, which transcribes the OCP with pseudospectral collocation and, instead of a Newton or SQP solve, integrates a primal--dual gradient flow of a Powell--Hestenes--Rockafellar augmented Lagrangian to compute a solution. Because the flow is stiff, this paper designs a linearly implicit integrator with a Gauss--Newton metric, momentum, and a merit-based step controller that keeps the augmented Lagrangian monotone. Abstract: Executing heavy-duty physical manipulation in unpredictable environments remains a major challenge for quadrupedal robots lacking dedicated manipulators. This paper presents SOMA, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for whole-body non-prehensile manipulation of multi-object stacks using a quadruped robot. articles.title: When a robot can trust reversing wind to find an odour source
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20970v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A wind-derived heading can guide a robot towards an odour source even after the wind reverses, but its reliability depends on the plume's transport history. On a quadruped initially facing the source, holding the initial heading reached it in every reversing-wind trial, whereas comparison controllers never settled there. An exact geometric condition links heading correctness to net odour transport, and simulations separate sensing error from departures from nominal flow. Where the alternating wind directions are too close for reversal alone to produce wrong-side headings, the wrong-side rate rises from 1.0% under uniform transport to 4.7% in a stochastic flow. Re-acquiring headings from new odour contact improves simulated search when contact is intermittent. These results identify distinct requirements for wind-guided search: a heading supported by the transport geometry and sufficient intermittent contact to replace it.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20998v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Passive human videos of everyday activity offer robots access to a massive amount of human experience without requiring a demonstration for each task. However, using this experience requires recovering knowledge from unstructured video recordings and adapting it to a different body (i.e., the robot). To overcome these challenges, we present mobile code-as-policy (MoCaP), an agentic framework that turns passive human video recordings into guidance for an end-to-end mobile manipulation policy. MoCaP extracts spatial memory and cues of how people prepare to interact with objects, which inform navigation and the search for a manipulation-ready configuration. Guided by passive human experience and current observations, MoCaP uses a closed-loop code-as-policy to coordinate planning and tool use primitives to solve motions under the robot's geometry and kinematic constraints. articles.title: Slip-Induced Fall Suppression During Cornering for a Remotely Operated Motorcycle with a Rear-Wheel-Swing Mechanism
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.21089v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Slip-induced falls when riding motorcycles are difficult to avoid even for expert riders and represent a major cause of single-vehicle accidents. Despite their prevalence, no practical solution has yet been proposed to suppress this phenomenon. We previously introduced a motorcycle model applicable to systems with both front- and rear- wheel steering. In this paper, we extend that model and formulate the suppression of slip-induced falls as an optimization problem that distributes assistive control inputs according to vehicle speed and road surface conditions. To evaluate the proposed method, we developed a remotely operated motorcycle and conducted experiments under two scenarios: slalom driving on a low-friction surface at 5.5 m/s, and turning maneuvers on synthetic ice to simulate driving over manholes on rainy days. The results demonstrate that our approach successfully suppresses falls under these challenging conditions.

articles.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
articles.content: Personalization is essential for general-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction. We introduce LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark for preference learning in embodied agents. LIBERO-PeRM studies five questions: 1) how policies follow preferences in zero-shot settings; 2) how they learn single preferences from demonstrations; 3) how efficiently they acquire preferences as demonstrations increase; 4) how learned preferences generalize across layouts and tasks; and 5) how policies compose preferences and behave under conflicts. We propose a controlled formulation and taxonomy of observable preferences in simulation, covering motion, skill, and user-profile choices. This formulation is restricted to language-expressible preferences that can be instantiated in LIBERO without changing the task goal, evaluated automatically, and reused across tasks. Building on LIBERO, our procedural pipeline generates paired demonstrations with and without preferences. We create five task suites (312 tasks) with high-quality demonstrations, rich metadata, and preference-satisfaction metrics. Experiments show that current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization, while SFT makes preferences learnable. Mixed training achieves better no-preference retention than sequential adaptation and improves performance with contextual prompts compared with preference-only training, but can weaken motion-preference learning; preference generalization, decomposition, and conflict handling remain difficult. The code, datasets, and demos can be found on the project website: https://libero-perm.github.io/.

articles.title: Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers
articles.content: We introduce Gen4P, a unified framework for recovering 4D geometry and motion from monocular video. We show that a pretrained video generator can be repurposed into a feed-forward 4D perceiver without iterative denoising. Building on on-demand querying, Gen4P processes clean video latents in a single encoder pass and predicts the requested 4D attributes through a lightweight cross-attention decoder. The on-demand query formulation enables flexible spatial sampling, and our proposed continuous-time queries further provide temporal flexibility. To strengthen geometric knowledge, we propose a straightforward plug-in solution by incorporating a pretrained video-depth LoRA as a frozen geometry prior, improving overall performance without adding extra trainable parameters. Gen4P achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on tasks of 3D point tracking, video depth and camera pose estimation. Qualitative results on in-the-wild videos illustrate its capability of tracking complex motion while maintaining the delicate structure. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of video generative pretraining for unified 4D perception. See https://gen4p.github.io for more visual results.

articles.title: Which Tokens to Merge? Diffusion Dynamics for Efficient Image Generation
articles.content: Token merging has emerged as an effective training-free strategy for accelerating diffusion models by reducing redundant token computation while minimizing generation degradation. A key challenge is determining which tokens can be safely merged and which should be preserved for subsequent computation. Existing method addresses this by preserving prompt-aligned foreground regions, thereby protecting semantically relevant structures. However, this text-relevance criterion overlooks background objects, local details that are not explicitly mentioned in the prompt, leading to degraded structural coherence. In this work, we propose Dynamics-aware Token Merging (DaTMe), a training-free framework that grounds token merging in the underlying diffusion dynamics. Our key insight is that token importance should reflect whether a token remains unresolved during denoising and whether it carries structural information. To this end, DaTMe constructs a dynamics- aware importance map from the Tweedie denoised estimate. The map combines a temporal signal, measuring inter-step changes in the predicted clean image, with a structural signal, capturing local high-frequency content such as boundaries and fine details. Using this map, DaTMe adaptively assigns tokens into merging roles under a given compression ratio: important tokens are preserved as anchors, while tokens that are both temporally stabilized and structurally homogeneous are selected as safe merge candidates. Experiments on PixArt-a and FLUX demonstrate that DaTMe maintains visual fidelity across the entire image, highlighting diffusion dynamics as an effective token-level merging decision in efficient generation. Our code is available at https://github.com/SeungJuCha/DaTMe.

articles.title: SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers
articles.content: Diffusion and flow models generate a sample over iterative steps, each a full pass through a large network, and that pass dominates generation cost. Training-free caching accelerates them by reusing activations from recent evaluations instead of recomputing them. Dynamic caching methods decide when to refresh by accumulating a cheap probe of the network input into a staleness signal and spending a fresh evaluation once it crosses a threshold. They perform hard caching: the signal is a binary switch between refresh and reuse, and every step, fresh or cached, advances by the prescribed step size. We observe that the signal carries much more than this switch. How far it sits below the threshold, its headroom, predicts the error induced by reuse. We propose SoftCache, which performs soft caching: instead of a binary switch, the headroom sets how far each cached step goes. Where the headroom is large, the sampler jumps past several scheduled nodes, and as a refresh nears, its steps shrink back toward the original step. These adaptive jumps may land between the scheduled nodes, taking the sampler off its fixed grid. SoftCache requires no training and adds no per-backbone settings: on FLUX for images and on HunyuanVideo and Wan2.1 for video, at speedups from $3.5\times$ to $6.9\times$, it is ahead of every baseline on all four fidelity metrics.

articles.title: Value as Memory: Online Value-Guided Post-training for General Robot Policies
articles.content: Real-world post-training of generalist robot policies faces two challenges: partial observability makes action selection ambiguous, while offline post-training methods delay feedback from deployment experience. We present Value as Memory (VaM), a framework that addresses these challenges through value caching and online real-world reinforcement learning (RL). Value caching conditions actions on recent value predictions as task-progress memory, while online updates enable timely policy improvement by combining offline demonstrations, off-policy interventions, and on-policy rollouts for sample-efficient adaptation. As a result, VaM transitions from offline RL warmup to online autonomous learning with sparse rewards. Across long-horizon tasks involving deformable objects and contact-rich manipulation, VaM yields a mean absolute success-rate gain of $29.4\%$ with value caching, while achieving a $32.8\%$ gain with online autonomous learning over matched offline training. The evaluated online schedule performs $8\times$ as many policy iterations under the same gradient-step budget, with more than $2\times$ lower recorded time per gradient step with concurrent data collection and training.
